title: Need some recomendations
author: Professional_Lion373
selftext:
I want to use Claude Code to try to bring my dream game to life, but I’ve reached a bit of a knowledge barrier when it comes to deciding which direction to take.

First, I want to make a JRPG in the style of **Star Ocean**.

Second, what engine would you recommend for a project like this, especially if I want to use an LLM alongside it?

Third, character design. I honestly have no idea where to even start in that area. Maybe I should create some kind of tool to help with it?

What would you guys recommend?

comments.author: ponderdiggums
comments.body:
I'm personally comfortable with Unity and Unreal and they work nicely with Claude so I always suggest those. Godot is supposed to be good too, but I haven't used it. 

I use Claude for engineering, and I use Astra to expand on my own art. AGY fills in when I run out of usage. 

For character design, I'd recommend against offloading that to the AI, at least at first. Even if you can't draw and just start with stick figures, create a dossier for characters you'd find interesting - sketch them out, write about their characteristics, their abilities, their background. It can be sketches and notes, that's fine - and you'll want more ideas than you'll ultimately use, and expect to make changes as you go. When you go on to story, you'll have a cast of character concepts you can adapt for your setting. Think about what goes into creating DnD characters

replies.author: Professional_Lion373
replies.body: I think I’ll try **Godot**. I don’t have a beefy machine or anything just a fairly average dell gaming notebook. Thanks for the insight

replies.author: DudeWithASweater
replies.body: I've been using godot and Claude and it works fantastic. Godot is very beginner friendly as well, definitely give it a shot.

comments.author: ProbablyDoesntLikeU
comments.body: Godot has been working pretty good, but I haven't used other engines besides a custom html5 engine

comments.author: Blackspyder99
comments.body: I think you should plug this exact question into whatever llm you like best.  That's what I did, tell it what you want to do and it will tell you what you need, if you have follow-up questions it will answer them.

comments.author: Fun-Term616
comments.body: Is your game 3d or 2d? Unity is great for 3D, godot isn't the best for 3d but it's super easy to use. Godot is for 2D games.
